title: Has a duplicate
prompt: Return True if any value appears at least twice in nums, otherwise False.
hints: Remember every value you have already seen.
A set answers 'have I seen this?' in expected O(1).
Check membership before adding the current value.

title: Count words
prompt: Return a dict mapping each word of the space-separated string text to how many times it occurs. Words are case-sensitive.
hints: Split the text into words first.
Use counts.get(word, 0) + 1 to update.
An empty string has no words: return {}.

title: First repeated character
prompt: Return the first character of s that appears for the second time while scanning left to right, or '' if no character repeats.
hints: You need to know, at each position, whether the character appeared earlier.
The first repeat is detected at the earliest second occurrence, not the earliest first occurrence.
Scan once with a set; return as soon as a character is already in it.

title: Most frequent value, smallest on ties
prompt: Return the value that occurs most often in the non-empty list nums. If several values share the highest count, return the smallest of them.
hints: Count every value first.
The tie rule is part of the answer: compare (count, value) carefully.
max over counts with key=lambda v: (counts[v], -v).

title: Reverse a list in place
prompt: Reverse the list nums in place with two pointers (no slicing or reversed()) and return it.
hints: Swap the outermost pair, then move inward.
Stop when the pointers meet or cross.
nums[i], nums[j] = nums[j], nums[i]

title: Pair with a target in a sorted list
prompt: nums is sorted ascending. Return [i, j] (i < j) with nums[i] + nums[j] == target using two pointers, or [] if none exists. If several pairs exist, return the one found by moving the smaller-sum side first (start from both ends).
hints: Start with the smallest and largest values.
A sum that is too small can only grow by moving the left pointer.
Return as soon as the sum matches; stop when left meets right.

title: Remove duplicates from a sorted list
prompt: nums is sorted ascending. Compact it in place so each value appears once, keeping order, and return the number of unique values k. (The checker reads only the return value.)
hints: Equal values are adjacent in a sorted list.
Keep a write index for the next unique value.
Write nums[read] when it differs from the last written value.

title: Is it a palindrome (letters and digits only)?
prompt: Return True if s reads the same forwards and backwards when you ignore every character that isn't a letter or digit and ignore letter case.
hints: Two pointers from both ends.
Skip characters that are not alphanumeric on each side.
Compare lower-cased characters; str.isalnum() helps.

title: Only round brackets
prompt: Return True if every '(' in s is closed by a later ')' and no ')' appears without a matching '('. Other characters are ignored.
hints: With one kind of bracket a counter is enough.
The count must never drop below zero.
Return depth == 0 at the end.

title: Undo with backspaces
prompt: In s, the character '#' deletes the previous surviving character (if any). Return the final text.
hints: Each character either adds to or removes from the end of the result.
A list used as a stack supports both in O(1).
Join the stack at the end.

title: Evaluate reverse Polish notation
prompt: tokens is a valid expression in reverse Polish notation using integers and the operators + - * /. Division truncates toward zero (like int(a / b)). Return the value.
hints: Numbers wait on a stack until an operator needs them.
An operator pops the right operand first, then the left.
int(a / b) truncates toward zero; a // b floors.

title: Days until a warmer day
prompt: For each day i in temps, return how many days you wait until a strictly warmer temperature, or 0 if none comes.
hints: A day is 'waiting' until a warmer day arrives.
Keep waiting days' indexes on a stack with decreasing temperatures.
When a warmer day arrives, pop and record i - index.

title: First index at or above target
prompt: nums is sorted ascending. Return the first index i with nums[i] >= target, or len(nums) if there is none. Don't use the bisect module.
hints: Keep the answer inside the half-open range [lo, hi].
If nums[mid] < target the answer is to the right of mid.
lo = mid + 1 in that case, otherwise hi = mid.

title: Range sums with a prefix array
prompt: Return a list with the sum of nums[i:j] for each [i, j] pair in queries (half-open ranges). Build a prefix array once.
hints: prefix[k] = sum of the first k values; prefix[0] = 0.
sum(nums[i:j]) = prefix[j] - prefix[i].
One pass to build, O(1) per query.

title: Climbing stairs
prompt: You climb n steps taking 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of distinct ways (n >= 0; there is 1 way to climb 0 steps).
hints: The last move was either 1 or 2 steps.
ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2).
Keep only the last two values.

title: Integer square root
prompt: Return the largest integer r with r * r <= x for a non-negative integer x, using binary search (no math.isqrt or ** 0.5).
hints: The predicate r*r <= x is true then false as r grows.
Search for the last r where it's true.
Search in [0, x + 1) and track the largest passing mid.

title: Count the inner-loop iterations
prompt: Return how many times the body of `for i in range(n): for j in range(i + 1, n): ...` runs, as a formula (no loops).
hints: For each i, the inner loop runs n - i - 1 times.
That sum is n(n-1)/2; return it as an int.

title: How many halvings?
prompt: Return how many times you can integer-halve n (n = n // 2) before it reaches 1, for n >= 1. This is floor(log2 n).
hints: Simulate the halving and count steps.
Stop when n becomes 1.
Alternatively: n.bit_length() - 1.

title: Pairs with a given difference
prompt: Return how many index pairs i < j satisfy abs(nums[i] - nums[j]) == k (k >= 1). Aim for O(n) expected time with a counter instead of checking every pair.
hints: For each value, count earlier values equal to value - k or value + k.
Keep a running count of values seen so far.
Add counts[value-k] + counts[value+k], then record value.

title: Classify a growth rate
prompt: steps[i] is the measured work at input size sizes[i] (sizes double each time). Return 'constant', 'linear' or 'quadratic' depending on whether the work stays the same, roughly doubles, or roughly quadruples between the last two measurements (use the ratio: < 1.5, < 3, otherwise).
hints: Look only at the last two measurements.
When size doubles, linear work doubles and quadratic work quadruples.
ratio = steps[-1] / steps[-2].

title: Move zeros to the end
prompt: Move all zeros in nums to the end in place, keeping the order of the non-zero values, and return nums.
hints: Write each non-zero value at the next write position.
Afterwards, every position from write onwards becomes 0.
Two loops over the same list; no new list.

title: Rotate right by k
prompt: Return a new list with nums rotated right by k positions (k >= 0 may exceed len(nums)). An empty list stays empty.
hints: Rotating by len(nums) changes nothing.
Reduce k modulo n, but only after checking n > 0.
The last k items move to the front.

title: Merge two sorted lists
prompt: a and b are sorted ascending. Return one sorted list with all their elements, in O(len(a) + len(b)) time (don't call sorted).
hints: Two read pointers, one per list.
Take the smaller front element each time.
Append whatever remains in either list at the end.

title: Reverse the words
prompt: Return the words of s in reverse order, separated by single spaces. Leading, trailing and repeated spaces disappear.
hints: Split without an argument handles runs of spaces.
Reverse the list of words.
Join with one space.

title: Sum of digits, recursively
prompt: Return the sum of the decimal digits of a non-negative integer n using recursion.
hints: A one-digit number is its own digit sum.
n % 10 is the last digit; n // 10 drops it.
solve(n) = n % 10 + solve(n // 10).

title: Power by squaring
prompt: Return base ** exp for an integer base and exp >= 0, using recursion that halves exp (O(log exp) multiplications).
hints: x^e = (x^(e//2))^2, times x if e is odd.
Compute the half power once and reuse it.

title: All permutations
prompt: Return every ordering of the distinct values in nums, in lexicographic order of positions chosen (i.e. the order produced by trying unused elements left to right).
hints: Build the permutation one position at a time.
Track which indexes are used; try unused ones left to right.
Record a copy when the permutation is full; undo after each choice.

title: Count paths in a grid
prompt: Return the number of paths from the top-left to the bottom-right of a rows × cols grid moving only right or down (rows, cols >= 1). Use memoised recursion or a DP.
hints: A path to (r, c) arrives from above or from the left.
paths(r, c) = paths(r-1, c) + paths(r, c-1); the first row and column have 1 path.
Memoise with lru_cache or fill a table row by row.

title: Reverse a linked list (as values)
prompt: values describes a singly linked list. Build the nodes, reverse the links in place (no reversed() on the values), and return the reversed values.
hints: Keep previous, current, and the saved next node.
Point current.next at previous, then step both forward.
previous ends as the new head.

title: Middle node
prompt: Return the value of the middle node of the non-empty list described by values. For an even length, return the second of the two middle nodes. Use slow/fast pointers.
hints: Move slow one step and fast two steps.
Stop when fast can't take two steps.
Slow is then at the middle (second middle for even lengths).

title: Remove the nth node from the end
prompt: Remove the nth node from the end (1 = last) of the list described by values, in one pass with a dummy head, and return the remaining values. 1 <= n <= len(values).
hints: A dummy node handles removing the head.
Move a lead pointer n+1 steps ahead of a trailing pointer, starting both at the dummy.
Advance both until lead is None; trailing.next is the node to remove.

title: Where does the cycle start?
prompt: values describes a list whose last node links back to index pos (or pos = -1 for no cycle). Return the index of the node where the cycle begins, or -1, using O(1) extra space (Floyd's algorithm).
hints: First detect a meeting point with slow/fast pointers.
Then move one pointer back to the head; advance both one step at a time.
They meet at the cycle entry. Map nodes to indexes to answer.

title: Hot potato
prompt: Players stand in a circle in the order given. Repeatedly pass the potato k times (move the front player to the back k times), then remove the player holding it (the new front). Return the order in which players are removed.
hints: A deque rotates cheaply: popleft then append.
After k passes, the front player is removed.
Repeat until the deque is empty.

title: Distances from a start node
prompt: graph maps each node (a string) to a list of neighbours. Return a dict of the BFS distance (number of edges) from start to every reachable node.
hints: The start is at distance 0.
A neighbour seen for the first time is one further than the current node.
Use a deque; a node is 'seen' when it gets a distance.

title: Sliding-window maximum
prompt: Return the maximum of every contiguous window of size k in values (1 <= k <= len(values)), in O(n) using a deque of indexes.
hints: Drop indexes that have left the window from the front.
Before pushing i, drop indexes with values <= values[i] from the back.
The front of the deque is the window's maximum once i >= k - 1.

title: Recent calls counter
prompt: times is a strictly increasing list of request times in milliseconds. For each request, return how many requests (including itself) happened in the inclusive window [t - 3000, t].
hints: Keep the recent request times in a queue.
Before counting, drop times older than t - 3000 from the front.
The queue length is the answer for t.

title: Sort by length, then alphabetically
prompt: Return words sorted by length ascending; words of equal length are sorted alphabetically.
hints: A tuple key compares the first element, then the second.
The key is (len(word), word).
sorted(words, key=...).

title: Counting sort for small ints
prompt: Sort nums, whose values are integers from 0 to 9, using counting (no sorted or .sort).
hints: Count how many times each digit appears.
Then emit each digit count times, in order.
counts = [0] * 10.

title: Top k frequent words
prompt: Return the k most frequent words, most frequent first; ties are broken alphabetically.
hints: Count each word.
Sort the distinct words by (-count, word).
Take the first k.

title: Count inversions
prompt: Return the number of index pairs i < j with nums[i] > nums[j], in O(n log n) using merge sort.
hints: Split, count inversions in each half, then count across halves while merging.
When you take an element from the right half, every remaining left element is larger.
Add len(left) - i at that moment.

title: The value without a partner
prompt: Every value in nums appears exactly twice except one. Return that value using XOR (O(1) extra space).
hints: x ^ x == 0 and x ^ 0 == x.
XOR every value together.
Order doesn't matter: XOR is commutative.

title: Is it a power of two?
prompt: Return True if the integer n is a positive power of two (1, 2, 4, …), using a bit trick.
hints: A power of two has exactly one set bit.
n & (n - 1) clears the lowest set bit.
So n > 0 and n & (n - 1) == 0.

title: Count set bits from 0 to n
prompt: Return a list whose i-th entry is the number of 1 bits in i, for every i from 0 to n, in O(n) using the relation bits(i) = bits(i >> 1) + (i & 1).
hints: bits(0) = 0.
Shifting right drops the last bit; add it back with i & 1.
Fill the list in increasing i.

title: The missing number
prompt: nums contains n distinct numbers taken from 0..n (so exactly one is missing). Return the missing one in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
hints: The full range 0..n has a known sum.
n = len(nums); expected = n(n+1)/2.
Or XOR all indexes and values together.

title: Brute-force oracle: count equal pairs
prompt: Return how many index pairs i < j have nums[i] == nums[j], by checking every pair (this is the oracle; clarity beats speed).
hints: Two nested loops over i < j.
Count the pairs where values match.
j starts at i + 1.

title: Fast version of the same count
prompt: Same contract as the oracle: count pairs i < j with nums[i] == nums[j], but in O(n) expected time.
hints: Each new value pairs with every earlier equal value.
Keep counts of values seen so far.
Add counts[value] before incrementing it.

title: Maximum subarray sum (all-negative safe)
prompt: Return the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray of nums (len(nums) >= 1). All-negative input must return its largest element.
hints: Track the best sum of a subarray ending at the current index.
Either extend the previous subarray or start fresh at the current value.
Initialise with nums[0], not 0.

title: Which inputs break it?
prompt: buggy(nums) returns max(nums) - min(nums) but crashes on empty input. Return the list of indexes into inputs for which calling max(x) - min(x) would raise (i.e. the empty lists).
hints: Which input makes max() raise?
Loop over inputs with their indexes.
Collect i where the list is empty.
